answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.8.2026) The Commission continues to attach great importance to ensuring a smooth implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)1. In order to ensure this, the Commission has carried out a comprehensive technical review of the IT system which is an independent module of the TRACES2 platform, established by Regulation (EU) 2017/6253, and its architecture. On that basis the Commission introduced targeted improvements to enhance the processing capacity, data handling, operational resilience, and user friendliness of the system4. Regarding contingency arrangements, Article 33(3)(b) mandates the Commission to establish rules for the functioning of the IT system, including contingency arrangements in the event of the unavailability of its functionalities. The Implementing Act laying down these provisions was adopted on 13 July 20265. Regarding administrative burden and risks of disruptions, the simplifications agreed by colegislators in December 20256 aim to concentrate on the submissions at the first placing on the market, with the introduction of a simplified one-off declaration for micro and small primary operators and removing the obligation of submission for downstream actors. These measures will significantly reduce the data load on the IT System. Moreover, the Commission published on 4 May 2026 the Simplification Review of EUDR7 – a package of measures designed to make implementation more practical, efficient and inclusive, including an overview Report and updated Guidance and Frequently Asked Questions. A Delegated Act updating the product scope of EUDR was also adopted on 13 July 2026. The measures taken since 2023 reduce expected compliance costs by about 75% compared to the original EUDR requirements. 1 Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making
